candidates: When modifying logic in a function, update any inline comments that described the old behavior to accurately reflect the new intent. A comment that contradicts the current code (e.g., saying 'avoid X' when the code now explicitly does X) is more harmful than no comment at all.

When building a string by concatenating with an optional-chained expression (e.g., `a + b?.method()`), guard against the `undefined` case explicitly rather than relying on optional chaining alone — string concatenation will happily produce `'value undefined'` if the optional chain resolves to `undefined`. Use a conditional instead, e.g., `b ? `${a}\n${b.method()}` : a`.
